title: Add Kotlin mobile RAG samples with compact tool-calling adapter and docs
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Mobile-first teams frequently ask for a compact, battery-friendly reference for building retrieval-augmented agents on Android/iOS using Kotlin Multiplatform. This PR adds a small set of opinionated examples and an accompanying docs quickstart that demonstrate: 1) performing client-side retrieval with an incremental index, 2) calling external tools (calendar, web-search shim) via a lightweight tool-calling adapter over WebSocket, 3) streaming and resumable responses (partial-response resume), and 4) offline-first UX patterns (local cache + optimistic UI).

What this PR includes (single continuous description): Adds a Kotlin Multiplatform mobile sample (android/ios targets) named "mobile-rag-lite" that contains a compact runtime binding to the Redwood API, a Ktor-based WebSocket tool-bridge shim (server example), and a Quickstart doc under docs/quickstarts/mobile-rag-lite.md. The quickstart walks through creating an incremental vector index using the embedded store, wiring the client to call the Redwood hosted API, and wiring tool-calls (calendar and http-search) that are proxied through a tiny Node/Ktor shim for demo purposes. The example emphasizes low-power batching, token-aware timeouts, and fallback policies for flaky networks.

Checklist: - [x] Kotlin Multiplatform sample scaffold (android + ios simulator) - [x] Compact SDK binding (Kotlin) that mirrors Redwood client call patterns - [x] Tool-calling adapter sample (WebSocket + HTTP bridge) - [x] Quickstart docs + runbook for CI smoke tests - [x] Unit tests for adapter and index helpers - [x] Telemetry hooks example (metric counters + session traces) - [x] Licence and README updated

Commit summary: "Initial kotlin multiplatform scaffold and samples" (adds the project structure and core bindings), "Add ws tool-bridge and demo server" (Ktor and Node examples used for local dev), "Quickstart docs and runbook" (docs + CI smoke definitions), "Fix telemetry and timeouts based on review feedback".

Changed areas (high level): - mobile-rag-lite/ (new KMM project with sample app, README and tests) - tools/ws-tool-bridge/ (Ktor server + minimal Node shim for quickstart) - docs/quickstarts/mobile-rag-lite.md (step-by-step quickstart) - docs/snippets/kotlin-bindings.md (API snippets and usage patterns) - .github/workflows/mobile-smoke.yml (CI smoke runner that uses Android emulator and iOS simulator stubs) - samples/testdata/inc-index/ (small seed corpus and test prompts) - license/ NOTICE updates

Small illustrative snippet (inlined for reviewers): "// client: perform incremental index upsert
val idx = LocalIndex.open(context)
idx.upsert("doc-1", text = "Release notes for Q1")
val emb = redwoodClient.embeddings.embedText("user query")
val hits = idx.search(emb, topK = 4)
val prompt = PromptBuilder.withContext(hits).withUser("What changed in Q1?")
redwoodClient.chat.stream(prompt, onDelta = { delta -> render(delta) })"

Review conversation (summary as a single continuous string): Reviewer Ethan Ross: "Nice compact layout — main ask is to make the tool bridge auth optional and document the security caveats. Also please avoid shipping demo API keys in the repo." Author reply (Priya): "Updated to require a local .env for demo keys and added a clear SECURITY.md section in the tool-bridge explaining KMS/HSM options for Private deployments. Removed all placeholder keys." Reviewer Marina Kovács: "Please add a short paragraph in the quickstart about batching and token-based timeouts for mobile networks." Author reply: "Added a dedicated section 'Mobile batching and timeouts' with recommended defaults and links to Optimize tooling." Reviewer Jonah Li: "CI flakes on emulator boot seen in run 2, can we shorten emulator setup and run a headless smoke mode?" Author reply: "Added emulator warmup in workflow and a headless smoke path; tests moved to parallel jobs to reduce timeouts." Ethan follow-up: "Approved after the docs and security notes landed."

CI summary and checks: - unit-tests (Kotlin): pass - lint (ktlint + detekt): pass - docs-spellcheck: pass - smoke-mobile (emulator): pass after wobble fix - e2e-sample-toolbridge: flaky-> rerun-> pass

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main once reviewers approved and CI green. Release notes: "Add Kotlin mobile RAG quickstart and tool-calling adapter (mobile-rag-lite). Includes KMM sample app, WS tool bridge demo, and quickstart docs describing offline-first indexing and tool-calling patterns."

How to run locally (condensed): 1) cd mobile-rag-lite && ./gradlew :app:installDebug to launch Android sample (or use ios simulator target). 2) Start tools/ws-tool-bridge with LOCAL_DEMO_KEYS set and run npm run dev in node-shim for the HTTP tool proxies. 3) Follow docs/quickstarts/mobile-rag-lite.md for stepwise guide including index seeding and telemetry toggles.

Notes for maintainers: The Kotlin binding is intentionally compact and mirrors the JS/TS SDK ergonomics — keep parity but prefer idiomatic KMP naming. Telemetry hooks are pluggable via a MetricsAdapter interface. This PR purposely avoids shipping production auth for the bridge and documents recommended production deployments (Private controller + KMS).
